references.text: In the preceding verse, John the Baptist points out Jesus as "the Lamb of God" — this is the testimony that the two disciples hear and which causes them to follow Jesus ([ref:Joh 1:36|John 1:36]).

John the Baptist's first proclamation of Jesus as "the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world" ([ref:Joh 1:29|John 1:29]) is the background for the testimony that the two disciples now respond to.

After the two disciples began following Jesus, he turned and asked what they were seeking. They stayed with him that day — this is the immediate continuation of their following ([ref:Joh 1:38-39|John 1:38-39]).
One of the two disciples who heard John speak and followed Jesus is identified as Andrew, Simon Peter's brother ([ref:Joh 1:40|John 1:40]).
The pattern of people hearing testimony about Jesus and then following him continues throughout the calling narrative: Philip and Nathanael follow after ([ref:Joh 1:43-45|John 1:43-45]).
John the Baptist's words "He must increase, but I must decrease" ([ref:Joh 3:30|John 3:30]) are concretely illustrated by his own disciples leaving him to follow Jesus.
Jesus' image of the sheep who know the shepherd's voice and follow him ([ref:Joh 10:4-5|John 10:4-5]), illustrates the same principle: those who hear, follow after.
"My sheep hear my voice … and they follow me" ([ref:Joh 10:27|John 10:27]) — this corresponds to the two disciples hearing the testimony about Jesus and following him.
Also in the Synoptics we find the pattern where disciples follow Jesus after his call, such as Simon and Andrew ([ref:Matt 4:19-20|Matthew 4:19-20]).
